title: LIVE UPDATES: 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits (Nov. 16, 2026)
summary: Leaders of member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) will attend Day 2 of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila. Here are the latest news and updates.

blocks.text: Indonesia president conveys apology to Singapore, Malaysia over wildfire haze

Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto apologized on Sunday to Singapore and Malaysia on behalf of his government for any impact that forest fires in Indonesia may have had on their people, and said authorities would continue to take firm action against companies linked to the blazes.

Prabowo added that Indonesian government has and will continue take firm actions on companies involved in forest fire cases while also preparing to establish a new body to strengthen forest-fire prevention.
The statements was conveyed by Prabowo during a session in ASEAN meeting, according to a statement from Indonesia's presidential palace on Sunday.
The Philippines' Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said on Sunday that Indonesia was very candid in expressing what it had done to address forest fires.
"The leaders also encouraged the ASEAN member states to prioritize the ratification of the ASEAN Coordinating Center on Transboundary Haze Pollution Control," Lazaro told a news briefing.
Indonesia has been battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years, with large swathes of land scorched, mainly on the islands of Sumatra, Borneo and Papua. — Reuters

QC orders bars, karaoke venues, spas to close at midnight during ASEAN 2026

Bars, karaoke venues, spas, massage parlors, internet cafes and other businesses in Quezon City covered by the SAFE SEAL Ordinance must close at midnight during the ASEAN Summit, the city government said.

In a statement, the Quezon City government said that the mandatory midnight closure is part of heightened security measures during the summit, which will be held in the Philippines from November 15 to 21.
"Mayor Joy Belmonte signed Executive Order No. 42 requiring establishments covered by the city’s SAFE SEAL Ordinance to close by midnight, subject to specified exemptions," the LGU said.

According to the Quezon City government, the Stops All Forms of Exploitation (SAFE) Seal is "is a voluntary certification granted to business establishments that promote and implement safety and protection measures against all forms of exploitation, including human trafficking."
Exemptions

The LGU said that while hotels, resorts, apartelles, tourist inns, motels, pension houses, homestays, and condominiums may remain open for accommodation purposes after midnight, any restaurants, restobars, drinking lounges, and similar venues within these properties must follow the ordinance and be closed by 12 a.m.
"Fast-food chains and convenience stores that operate 24/7 are also exempt from the closing requirement," the LGU said.
The Philippines is hosting the ASEAN Summit from November 15 to 21, 2026. — BM, GMA News
